seal.statement: canary-proof-reuse landed a recording path that could never run: writing a whole-corpus receipt pushes refs/lagrange-proofs/<contract>/<sha>, and git push runs the pre-push hook, which began linting every tracked file and would have re-run the whole corpus for a ref that carries no source at all. Measured 2026-09-18 on the published head b96b41f5b: the authority hung until the gate's own 60 s bound killed it, so no receipt was ever written and the canary kept re-proving (the fail-safe held, but the feature was inert). The hook already had the right precedent - a tag-only fast path for commits already on origin/main - and a receipt is exactly that shape: an annotated tag over a commit that is already proven and pushed. The fast path now admits refs/lagrange-proofs/* under the SAME ancestor test, so a receipt for a commit that is not on origin/main still gates, and a receipt among the ref lines of a source push cannot exempt it. With the arm in place the same recording took 7.5 s and the canary's decision for that sha flipped to needed=false.

text: the pre-push fast path admits refs/lagrange-proofs/* beside refs/tags/* under the same origin/main ancestor test; three witnesses in the hook's behavioural harness (receipt-only push runs no content stage; a receipt for an unproven commit still gates; a receipt beside a branch gates on the branch), with the fixture gaining a bare remote whose main is the first commit so both answers are observable; the stage manifest records what the fast path proves. Verified end to end: recording the receipt for b96b41f5b took 7.5 s where it previously hung past 120 s, the ref is on origin, and the canary decision for that sha is now needed=false while an unproven sha stays needed=true

round 1 REJECT (B1): the hook arm does not reach the path that records. recordCorpusProof runs INSIDE the gate for the sha being pushed, which by construction is not yet an ancestor of origin/main, so the ancestor test fails and the nested receipt push still re-enters the gate - reproduced twice against a real bare remote, including the in-place branch under the gate's own exported env (identity, unused-files, lint over every tracked file, ratchets, test-stage). The 7.5 s measurement was a manual record of a sha already on origin/main, so 'verified end to end' was true for the manual path and false for the gate's own; canary reuse stayed inert for a normal push. Safety enumeration otherwise clean: 12 hostile ref shapes all answered correctly, fail-closed when origin/main is absent or the fetch is offline, mixed pushes gated on the branch, no widening in kind over the pre-existing tag arm; mutations a/b/c red; end-to-end against a fake remote confirmed <1 s with the arm and a 25 s timeout without it. Non-blocking: N1 pre-existing first-local-sha weakness with newly created refs, N2 non-commit targets gate opaquely, N3 receipt trust rests on remote ref protection, N4 stderr leak, N6 no negative witness for the -stage namespace, N7 stage id still says tag-only.

round 1 repair, in two parts because the hook arm alone cannot reach the recorder: the gate now DEFERS when the sha is not yet an ancestor of origin/main (a fast merge-base check, so it never re-enters the gate and never waits for the 60 s bound), and scripts/publish-head.js records after the push it has already verified, reading the gate run's own proof-scope file - witnessed in a node:test companion (the tap-library publish test cannot be selected by --test-name-pattern) for the recorded case, a cone proof, another sha, missing keys, a non-boolean fullCorpus, no scope file at all, a bounded spawn and a refused recording. The quest statement is corrected to say exactly which path was proved by measurement

round 2 APPROVE: the B1 repair is in the right place (recording moved to where the commit is published rather than relaxing the gate for an unpublished commit's objects), witnessed and mutation-sensitive; deferral exercised against real git (3 ms, authority never spawned, no receipt on the remote), 16-case safety enumeration reproduced exactly on a clean fixture (the verifier's own round-1 fixture had drifted because its stubbed materializer advanced the fake remote), hook mutations a/b/c red, publisher mutations g/h red, and four independent reasons why a stale or planted scope cannot mint a receipt (fresh mkdtemp worktree per publish, test-output gitignored and unlistable from the commit, the gate's test stage the only writer with the publisher's push skipping tests, and a red gate throwing before the push). All four constraints hold. Non-blocking: R1 the publisher call site unwitnessed, R2 not exception-safe, R3 the deferral does not fetch while the hook's arm does, R4 writeProofScope writes fullCorpus before the verdict (pre-existing, epic), R5 the hasOwn clauses called redundant, plus the round-1 carry-overs with N1 kept for the epic.

round 2 follow-ups R1, R2 and R5 taken: the publisher's call site is now witnessed end to end in the tap suite (a stub authority and a gate stub that writes the proof scope record their argv into the same file as the hook lines, so the receipt is proved to be recorded AFTER the verified push, for the published sha; the fixture gains the .gitignore the real repository has, or the publisher's mutation guard fires first), the spawn is wrapped so a throwing runner is reported and cannot fail a finished publish, and R5 turns out NOT to be redundant - the own-property clauses are what reject an inherited fullCorpus, now witnessed by a polluted-prototype case. Deleting the call site or the hasOwn clauses each turns a witness red.

follow-ups (not this quest): R3 the gate's deferral reads the local origin/main without fetching while the hook's arm fetches, so a hand-forwarded tracking ref can make the gate try and the hook gate the receipt push - bounded at 60 s, no wrong receipt; R4 writeProofScope writes fullCorpus:true before the corpus verdict, so the scope means 'the corpus was selected' and the publisher is safe only because a red gate throws first - the same pre-verdict artifact is what ci uploads for the canary; N1 the first local sha is the tree under proof, so a receipt refspec ahead of a newly created branch ref gates the wrong tree (pre-existing, identically reachable via refs/tags/*, and refs/heads/main is structurally protected); N6 the -stage namespace boundary has no negative witness; N7 the stage id still reads tag-only-fast-path.
